answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% cost reduction and the primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew. With the assembly line at 94% and zero buffer, delivery risk cannot absorb a switch or a lapse. Switching vendors (memory_c2) could cut cost but introduces onboarding risk the line cannot tolerate right now. Adding a second source (memory_c3 pattern) is a resilience play, not a cost play, and would not meet the 18% target alone. Deferring (memory_c5) is not viable because there is no auto-renew clause; a lapse would halt supply. Renegotiating with the incumbent leverages memory_c4 (benchmarking recovered margin on price and payment terms) and memory_c6 (multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope). I pull memory_c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor is a credible BATNA for the negotiation, and memory_c4 to confirm the benchmarking approach yielded material concessions. If verification confirms both, I open a renegotiation with the incumbent anchored on a multi-year term (per c6) and market-rate benchmarks (per c4), using the low-cost vendor as leverage, targeting the 18% reduction while preserving the existing integration and delivery cadence.
